text: What does ORS do in diarrhoea?
response_text:
What does ORS do in diarrhoea?
Oral rehydration solution (ORS) is a mixture of clean water, salts and sugar. In diarrhoea the body loses water and salts; ORS is absorbed in the small intestine and replaces them, which WHO describes as the cornerstone of treating dehydration from diarrhoea. WHO also advises continuing to eat (and breastfeeding infants) and, for children, zinc supplements as advised by a health worker. Get medical help urgently if there is blood in the stool, the person cannot drink, is very sleepy, has sunken eyes or is passing very little urine. [1]

text: Are generic medicines as effective as branded ones?
response_text:
Are generic medicines as effective as branded ones?
In India every medicine, branded or generic, must meet the same quality standards under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. A generic with the same active ingredients, strength, dosage form and release type is expected to work the same way; it is usually cheaper because it carries no brand-marketing cost. Inactive ingredients (fillers, colours) can differ. For a few medicines where small differences matter (for example thyroid medicines, blood thinners and anti-epileptics), doctors may prefer that you stay on one brand. Always confirm any switch with your doctor or pharmacist. [1]

The NHS advises that antacids work best taken with or soon after food, when indigestion and heartburn are most likely, and that their effect may last longer when taken with food. Antacids can affect how well other medicines work, so the NHS advises not to take other medicines within 2 to 4 hours of an antacid. Antacids are not meant for regular long-term use: speak to a doctor if you need them often, and ask a pharmacist first if you are pregnant, have kidney, liver or heart problems, are on a low-salt diet, or are choosing one for a child under 12.
